content: Metaproterenol is a medication prescribed to prevent and treat wheezing, shortness of breath, and difficulty breathing caused by asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and other lung diseases. It works by relaxing and opening the air passages in the lungs, making it easier to breathe. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Metaproterenol is available in various forms, including tablets, syrup, and solutions or aerosols for oral inhalation. It is typically used as needed to relieve symptoms or every 3-4 hours to prevent symptoms. When taken orally, it is usually administered three or four times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take metaproterenol exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. If you are using metaproterenol as needed for asthma attacks, do not exceed 12 puffs per day. While metaproterenol helps control symptoms of asthma and other lung diseases, it does not cure them. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before using the metaproterenol inhaler for the first time, read the written instructions provided with it. Ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to demonstrate the proper technique, and practice using the inhaler in their presence. To use the inhaler, follow these steps: 1. Shake the inhaler well. 2. Remove the protective cap. 3. Exhale completely through your nose while keeping your mouth closed. 4. Place the open end of the mouthpiece well into your mouth, past your front teeth, and close your lips tightly around it. 5. Take a slow, deep breath through the mouthpiece while simultaneously pressing down on the container to release the medication into your mouth. Ensure the mist enters your throat and is not blocked by your teeth or tongue. For young children, an adult may need to hold the child’s nose closed to ensure the medication is inhaled properly. 6. Hold your breath for 5-10 seconds, remove the inhaler, and exhale slowly through your nose or mouth. 7. If you are taking two puffs, wait two minutes and shake the inhaler well before taking the second puff. 8. Replace the protective cap on the inhaler. If you have difficulty inhaling the medication into your lungs, a spacer device may help. Consult your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist for guidance. Before taking metaproterenol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to metaproterenol or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription medications you are taking, especially atenolol, carteolol, labetalol, metoprolol, nadolol, phenelzine, propranolol, sotalol, theophylline, timolol, tranylcypromine, or other medications for asthma, heart disease, or depression. Also, inform them about any nonprescription medications, vitamins, or supplements you are using, including ephedrine, phenylephrine, phenylpropanolamine, pseudoephedrine, diet pills, or medications for colds and asthma. Check labels carefully and do not take these medications without consulting your doctor, even if you have used them without issues in the past. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had irregular heartbeat, increased heart rate, glaucoma, heart disease, high blood pressure, an overactive thyroid gland, diabetes, or seizures. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know. If you become pregnant while taking metaproterenol, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform the doctor or dentist that you are taking metaproterenol. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Metaproterenol may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: Tremor Nervousness Dizziness Weakness Headache Upset stomach Cough Dry mouth Throat irritation If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: Increased difficulty breathing Rapid or increased heart rate Irregular heartbeat Chest pain or discomfort If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Do not use the solution if it appears pink, yellow, darker than usual, or contains floating particles. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly; consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. Avoid puncturing the container and do not discard it in an incinerator or fire. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the victim has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 for emergency assistance. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order lab tests to monitor your response to metaproterenol. To alleviate dry mouth or throat irritation caused by inhalation, rinse your mouth with water, chew gum, or suck on sugarless hard candy after using the medication. Clean inhalation devices regularly. Once a week, remove the drug container from the plastic mouthpiece, wash the mouthpiece with warm tap water, and dry it thoroughly. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
